overview: Sennen Cove is the first beach you reach heading north from Land’s End, about three kilometres along the coast. The beach sits below a small granite village at the southern end of Whitesand Bay, and the sand runs on northwards towards Gwenver at the far end of the bay.

It’s a working cove as well as a holiday beach: the RNLI lifeboat station here dates back to 1853, and next to it a restored round building that once housed a winch for hauling boats out of the water is now a gallery and shop.

expect.title: Surfing
expect.text: Sennen is a popular surf spot, a little more sheltered from the wind and swell than Gwenver further up the bay. It works at most stages of the tide except the very top.

expect.title: Facilities
expect.text: There’s a car park and a beach café by the sand, and surf equipment can be hired at the beach.

expect.title: The lifeboat station
expect.text: Volunteers run an all-weather lifeboat and an inshore boat from the station at the southern end of the beach.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: The village is on a short road off the A30 near Land’s End; the last stretch down to the beach is steep.

goodToKnow.label: Coast path
goodToKnow.text: The South West Coast Path passes through the village, so you can walk to Land’s End along the cliffs.
